solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Team on pitch is rocking, wickets taken now and then? (7,4)

indicatorNotes.rocking: something rocking is shaken about, so its letters are jumbled

blocks.note: W = wickets, as on a cricket scorecard
anagram fodder, taken in with the rest
surface padding: it completes the phrase 'now and then' for the story

annotation.surface: A cricket commentator marvels at a lively pitch where wickets fall every so often.
annotation.walkthrough: The cricket words steer you to a cricket side, but Ipswich Town is an English football club. 'Now and then' reads as one phrase; only NOW is fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A football club counts as a team, and the clue hides that behind cricket words.

entries.clue: Overlap ultimately seen with celestial pair shifting? (7,7)

annotation.definition: Overlap ultimately seen with celestial pair shifting?

indicatorNotes.ultimately: ultimately points to the final letter of overlap
indicatorNotes.shifting: letters that shift move out of their order

annotation.surface: Two heavenly bodies drift until they overlap in the sky.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: in a partial eclipse the sun and moon, a celestial pair, shift until they only partly overlap.
annotation.definitionFit: Read straight, the clue describes the event: sun and moon move across each other and overlap only in part.

entries.clue: Little bit pale when cut (4)

indicatorNotes.when cut: a word that is cut is trimmed short, so the final letter of WHITE is sliced off

blocks.note: WHITE (pale) with its last letter cut off

annotation.surface: A small piece of something looks pale once sliced.
annotation.walkthrough: The word survives mainly in the phrase 'not a whit', meaning not at all.
annotation.definitionFit: An old word for the smallest amount, now found mostly in 'not a whit'.

entries.clue: Priest joins club in Church of England, observing religious vow (8)

indicatorNotes.joins: joins puts one piece beside the next
indicatorNotes.in: in puts the joined pair inside CE

blocks.note: CE = Church of England, split around the rest
Eli, the priest who raised Samuel

annotation.surface: A cleric takes up a post in the Anglican church and keeps his vows.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Joins' pairs the priest and the club first, and only then does 'in' put that pair inside the Church.
annotation.definitionFit: Celibacy is the vow of chastity taken by monks, nuns and Catholic priests, so someone keeping it is observing a religious vow.

entries.clue: You and I measure up? An insufficient amount (3,3)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom, backwards

blocks.note: a foot is a measure of length

annotation.surface: Two people wonder whether they meet the required standard, and fear they fall short.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Measure up' looks like one phrase about meeting a standard, but 'up' is working alone, turning WE FOOT upside down in this down entry.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: not enough in number is an insufficient amount.

entries.clue: Some bedfellow, I feel – for husband? (4)

indicatorNotes.Some: some of the words, not all, supply the answer

annotation.surface: Someone muses on who shares a husband's bed.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is loose, and the question mark admits it: the answer is the partner that goes with a husband.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by relation: the wife is the partner matched to a husband, the one he is for and who is for him.

entries.clue: Make improvements – righten when this happens? (4,3,7)

blocks.note: to vary how something is done, for the better
a riddle: shuffle the letters of THE RING and they spell RIGHTEN

annotation.surface: Someone suggests that improvements will set things right.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half is a riddle: RIGHTEN is what you get when you change THE RING, so the phrase gets a word-game meaning.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom from bell-ringing, where changes are the orders the bells sound in; it means to vary things, and literally to rearrange THE RING.

entries.clue: Cain, he? (5,6)

blocks.note: in Genesis, Cain, son of Adam and Eve, was the next human after his parents
a pronoun for someone neither speaking nor spoken to

annotation.walkthrough: Two senses from two worlds: Cain was the third human being in Genesis, and 'he' belongs to grammar's third person.
annotation.definitionFit: Cain was literally the third human to exist, and 'he' is the grammatical form for someone spoken about.

entries.clue: Statement of belief, religious relic perhaps? (7,2,5)

blocks.note: a tenet, one point of a creed
read literally: an object belonging to a religion

annotation.surface: A creed is set beside a holy relic.
annotation.walkthrough: The second sense reads 'article' as a physical object, so a relic becomes one; 'perhaps' flags that it is one example.
annotation.definitionFit: The phrase means a firmly held tenet, and read literally it is any object belonging to a faith, such as a relic.

entries.clue: Beer, dear, both good and bad (11)

blocks.note: bitter is a type of British ale

annotation.surface: A drinker's pint, and the darling beside them, both have their ups and downs.
annotation.walkthrough: Bitter is a British pale ale served in pubs.
annotation.definitionFit: Something bittersweet mixes pleasure with sadness, both good and bad.

entries.clue: Bird, one with head of black exists (4)

indicatorNotes.head of: the head of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: A bird watcher notes one with a black head.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests describing a bird's plumage; 'with' simply joins I to the next piece.
annotation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-billed wading bird.

entries.clue: Where brothers or sisters found energy feeding new baby (5)

indicatorNotes.feeding: E goes inside, as food goes into a mouth
indicatorNotes.new: a new version of BABY has its letters rearranged

annotation.surface: A family scene where a sibling gets a burst of energy from feeding the new baby.
annotation.walkthrough: Brothers and sisters look like siblings round a baby; here they are monks and nuns, and 'found' means 'are found'.
annotation.definitionFit: An abbey is where monks or nuns, religious brothers or sisters, live.

entries.clue: Food additive right behind cooker (4)

indicatorNotes.behind: R goes after, behind, the cooker

blocks.note: an Aga is a British range cooker

annotation.surface: Something spilled has ended up down the back of the stove.
annotation.walkthrough: An Aga is a heavy cast-iron range cooker, a fixture of British country kitchens and of crosswords.
annotation.definitionFit: Agar is a seaweed jelly used to thicken food.

entries.clue: Inexperienced politician (5)

blocks.note: a member of an environmentalist party

annotation.surface: A newcomer to politics.
annotation.walkthrough: It reads as one person, a novice politician, but the two words are separate definitions.
annotation.definitionFit: Unripe fruit is this colour, hence the sense of inexperience; the environmentalist party takes the colour of nature as its name.

entries.clue: Note priest provided, sent up (5)

indicatorNotes.sent up: in a down clue, sending something up reverses it

annotation.surface: A priest is written a note, on condition that it's mocked.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks musical at first; it is money.
annotation.definitionFit: A fiver is British slang for a five-pound banknote.

entries.clue: Bear or real cuckoo eaten by bear (8)

indicatorNotes.cuckoo: cuckoo means crazy, so the letters go wild

blocks.note: to tote is to carry, bear; it is split around the rest

annotation.surface: A fable in which a bird is swallowed by a bear.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bear' appears twice with two meanings: first put up with, then carry. The cuckoo is no bird but a signal to scramble REAL.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to bear an insult is to put up with it.

entries.clue: Man I go to town on beer initially! (6)

indicatorNotes.initially: initially takes the first letter of beer
indicatorNotes.on: I SHOP is placed on, after, the B

blocks.note: go to town = go shopping, shop

annotation.surface: Someone vows a big night out drinking.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Man' is a chess piece. 'Go to town on' looks like one idiom for splurging; the 'on' is split off to place the pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: In chess the pieces are called men, and a bishop is one of them.

entries.clue: Unknown figure couple invested in this rare diamond (8)

indicatorNotes.rare: rare means unusual, so THIS takes an unusual order

blocks.note: X = an unknown number, from algebra
to tie is to couple, join

annotation.surface: A jeweller describes a rare stone that a couple have sunk money into.
annotation.walkthrough: X and TIE go into the middle of SITH. 'Diamond' looks like the gem the couple bought; it is the anniversary.
annotation.definitionFit: Anniversaries take material names, and diamond marks sixty years, as in a diamond wedding or jubilee.

entries.clue: Fly in salad? (6)

blocks.note: a peppery leaf, called arugula in America

annotation.surface: A diner finds an insect in their salad.
annotation.walkthrough: The fly looks like an insect in your lunch; it is a verb, and the leaf is the British name for arugula.
annotation.definitionFit: The verb means to fly up fast, and the same word names a salad leaf.

entries.clue: Device attached to a killer gag? (8)

blocks.note: a muffler screwed onto the barrel of a gun

annotation.surface: A joke is played on an assassin.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gag' looks like a joke; it is the cloth that keeps someone quiet. The killer is the gun, not the gunman.
annotation.definitionFit: The word names the muffling tube fitted to a gun, and anything that stops speech, as a gag does.

entries.clue: Send for whole day (6)

annotation.surface: Someone is called in for a full day's work.
annotation.walkthrough: 'For' looks like a link, but it belongs to the definition 'Send for'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to send for someone is to call them to you.

entries.clue: Weapon held in parliament, first of all, for Westminster official? (4)

indicatorNotes.first of all: take the first of all the words

blocks.note: first letters of Weapon Held In Parliament

annotation.surface: Someone asks whether an arms-bearing official guards Parliament.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is also a weapon, which makes the surface doubly neat. In British politics the whip is the party officer who keeps MPs voting the party line.
annotation.definitionFit: A whip is a party official at Westminster who enforces voting discipline.

entries.clue: Pretty, I agree (5)

blocks.note: the adverb, as in pretty good, meaning fairly
a clipped British reply showing agreement

annotation.surface: Someone concurs that something is attractive.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pretty' looks like an adjective for looks; it is the adverb, as in pretty good.
annotation.definitionFit: The word means fairly, like pretty, and said on its own it is a British way to agree.

entries.clue: Resort for a Portuguese city (4)

annotation.surface: A holidaymaker picks a Portuguese city to stay in.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a holiday destination, and Faro is one, but here it means re-sort.
annotation.definitionFit: Faro is a city in the Algarve in southern Portugal.

entries.clue: Maple tree, more fabulous? (4)

blocks.note: ace = fabulous, with -R making the comparative

annotation.surface: A gardener rates a maple as more splendid.
annotation.walkthrough: The second sense treats slang 'ace' as an adjective with a comparative, a playful stretch the question mark owns.
annotation.definitionFit: It is the Latin genus name for maples, and also a jokey comparative of ace.

entries.clue: Capital nothing like that, pound invested (4)

blocks.note: so = like that, in that way
L = pound, from the Latin libra

annotation.surface: A financier puts a pound into capital, which isn't the done thing.
annotation.walkthrough: Capital, pound and invested all point to finance, but Capital is a city. L goes inside SO.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Norway's capital city, with 'Capital' dressed as money.

entries.clue: Don’t worry about the cost – travel restrictions lifted then? (4,4,4,2)

blocks.note: said of money lightly gained and lightly lost
read literally, arriving and leaving are both simple

annotation.surface: A traveller is relaxed about expense now that lockdown rules have gone.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half reads the proverb literally: with no travel restrictions, it is simple to arrive and simple to leave.
annotation.definitionFit: The saying shrugs off money lost as lightly as it came, and literally describes free movement.

entries.clue: Variety of starch often in eggy bread (6,5)

indicatorNotes.Variety of: a variety is a different arrangement of the letters

annotation.surface: A nutritional note about which kinds of starch turn up in eggy bread.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a food fact, and French toast is itself starchy, so the anagram hides in plain sight.
annotation.definitionFit: Eggy bread is the British name for bread soaked in egg and fried, which Americans call French toast.
